rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation is the prescribed signature: `impl<'d, D: Domain> Validator<'d, D> { pub fn check_inputs<O>(&self, inputs: &Fingerprinted<D, O>) -> Result<bool, D::Error> }`. The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph.rs#impl[Validator<'d, D>]/fn[check_inputs]` declares exactly that signature and carries the {impl} marker. It delegates to `dependencies_are_current` (reached from the marked root, so it needs no marker of its own). That helper compares each saved dependency fingerprint, for nodes and for outgoing edges, with the current domain. It returns `Ok(false)` on a mismatch and propagates domain errors. The version-compatibility check is delegated to the caller and only cited (`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records.version_match`), so it is not an obligation here. The remaining text states observable behavior only, and the code does it.

behavioral: The subject has three behavioral obligations: compare each saved observation with the current domain, return `Ok(false)` when a fingerprint changed (and `Ok(true)` when none did), and propagate a domain error as `Err(D::Error)`. Version compatibility is delegated to the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records.version_match`. It is the caller's job, so it needs no test here.

Test coverage:
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[changing_one_criteria_input_does_not_invalidate_another]` saves two criteria that read different nodes, then changes one node's content. It asserts `check_inputs(&behavior)` is false and `check_inputs(&structure)` is true. That covers a changed node fingerprint giving false, an unchanged one giving true, and no cross-contamination between records.
- `contracts.rs#fn[dependency_resolution_failures_do_not_execute_or_replace_saved_answers]` covers a record with a `Node` dependency and an `OutgoingEdges` dependency.
  - `check_inputs` returns `Ok(true)` when nothing changed.
  - It returns `Ok(false)` after the edge set changes. The edges dependency is the second observation, so earlier unchanged observations do not mask a later change.
  - With `fail_read` set, it returns `Err("read")`. With `fail_edges` set, it returns `Err("edges")`. Both are asserted on a loaded record.
  - It also asserts that no execution or write happens and that the saved record is unchanged.
- `contracts.rs#fn[input_checking_and_execution_keep_separate_observations]` asserts `Ok(false)` for a changed node on a loaded record. The `reads` and `executions` assertions show that checking does not run the criterion or replace the saved observations.

The three tests cover node and edge observation kinds, changed and unchanged results, and error propagation. They assert on the actual return values, so I found no gap. `public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` only checks the exports and is not a behavioral test of this requirement.
